def overlap(a0,a1,b0,b1):

# time-weighted contingency: predicted speaker -> {ref speaker: overlap seconds}
from collections import defaultdict
contingency = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(float))

content.text:
Pulled real numbers before agreeing or disagreeing — checked our diarized output against the `.rttm` ground truth that ships with the fixtures. Here's what it actually shows:

**`meeting-15min.wav`** (the one legit single continuous 4-speaker meeting):
- Ground truth: 4 speakers
- Our pipeline predicted: **8 speaker clusters**
- Time-weighted cluster purity: **51.2%**

That means the diarizer is splitting real speakers into roughly 2× too many identities, and even the clusters it does form are only correct about half the time by overlap. That's not a "beta" number — that's a rough one. Given #300 just wired up speaker enrollment/auto-matching on top of this diarization output, this over-splitting will directly undermine that feature: an enrolled speaker will get correctly matched on some segments and missed on others because the diarizer itself keeps fragmenting them.

One more thing worth flagging: `meeting-30min.rttm` and `meeting-60min.rttm` list **61 and 66 "reference speakers"** respectively — not a real 30/60-min meeting, but a concatenation of the 15-min meeting plus dozens of unrelated VoxPopuli clips (`VP_xxxxx` speaker IDs) spliced in to pad duration. So those two fixtures aren't testing long-meeting diarization quality at all — they're testing something closer to "diarize an audio collage." Their purity numbers (35%/40%) shouldn't be read as representative of anything real.

So: transcription (Parakeet, 305× RTF) looks genuinely solid on the quick eyeball. Diarization speaker-clustering, on this one real fixture we have ground truth for, is weak enough that I wouldn't call it beta-ready as-is — I'd call the transcription beta-ready and the diarization pre-beta.

Want me to file a "SEE SOMETHING" issue on the diarization over-clustering with these numbers, and/or dig into why it's splitting speakers (clustering threshold, embedding drift over the recording, etc.)?

input.command:
unset GITHUB_TOKEN && gh issue create --repo gitrdunhq/Record-Suite \
  --title "[see-something] quality: diarization over-clusters speakers, ~51% purity on real fixture (FluidDiarizationPlugin.swift)" \
  --label "see-something,quality" \
  --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What's wrong

Ran the ProofHarness pipeline (`Tools/ProofHarness`) over the real fixtures in
`Data/diarization-fixtures/` (fast quality: Parakeet ASR + FluidDiarizationPlugin,
summarization skipped) and scored the diarized output against the checked-in `.rttm`
ground truth. On the one fixture that's a genuine single continuous meeting recording
(`meeting-15min.wav`, 4 real speakers per `meeting-15min.rttm`):

- Ground truth: **4 speakers**
- Predicted speaker clusters: **8**
- Time-weighted cluster purity: **51.2%**

i.e. the diarizer is splitting real speakers into roughly 2x too many identities, and
even the resulting clusters only match a single ground-truth speaker about half the
time by overlap duration. Per-cluster breakdown:

```
pred=  12 total=409.5s  -> best match ref=FEO072  (206.3s, purity 50%)
pred=  11 total=218.8s  -> best match ref=MEE071  (114.9s, purity 53%)
pred=  13 total=111.2s  -> best match ref=MEE073  ( 61.1s, purity 55%)
pred=   1 total= 73.3s  -> best match ref=FEO070  ( 31.2s, purity 43%)
pred=   5 total= 33.8s  -> best match ref=MEE073  ( 16.5s, purity 49%)
pred=   2 total= 29.5s  -> best match ref=MEE073  ( 20.5s, purity 69%)
pred=   4 total= 13.4s  -> best match ref=MEE073  (  4.6s, purity 34%)
pred=  10 total= 11.8s  -> best match ref=FEO070  (  6.5s, purity 55%)
```

## Why it matters

- #300 just wired up speaker enrollment + auto-matching on top of this diarization
  output (`EnrollSpeakerUseCase` / `MatchSpeakersUseCase`). If the diarizer keeps
  fragmenting a single real speaker into 2+ predicted IDs mid-meeting, an enrolled
  speaker will get correctly matched on some segments and silently missed on others
  — the auto-match feature can't outperform the diarization it sits on.
- This is real production code on real audio, not a mock/test artifact: the harness
  instantiates the actual `FluidDiarizationPlugin` (`Record-ML/Sources/MLInfrastructure/Diarization/FluidDiarizationPlugin.swift`)
  used by `AppAssembler`/`TranscriptionSubAssembler` in the shipping app.
- 51% purity with 2x over-splitting reads as pre-beta quality for the diarization
  sub-system specifically, even though transcription (Parakeet, ~305x RTF) looked solid.

## Caveat on the other two RTTM fixtures

`meeting-30min.rttm` and `meeting-60min.rttm` are NOT useful for this metric as-is —
they list 61 and 66 "reference speakers" respectively. They're not real single
30/60-minute meetings; they're the 15-min meeting concatenated with dozens of unrelated
VoxPopuli clips (`VP_xxxxx` speaker IDs) spliced in purely to pad duration for
transcription-length stress testing. Purity numbers computed against them (35%/40%)
aren't meaningful for diarization quality and should be ignored for this investigation
— `meeting-15min.wav` is the only fixture with a trustworthy ground truth for this.

## Suggested investigation

- `Record-ML/Sources/MLInfrastructure/Diarization/FluidDiarizationPlugin.swift` —
  check clustering/similarity threshold config passed into FluidAudio's diarizer;
  2x over-splitting is a classic symptom of a threshold set too strict (or embedding
  drift not being compensated for over the recording).
- Consider adding an automated DER/purity check to `Tools/ProofHarness` (there's
  already `.rttm` ground truth sitting unused next to the fixtures — `RunAll`/`List`
  just check for its *existence*, they don't score against it) so this kind of
  regression gets caught automatically instead of requiring a manual pass.
- If a real single-meeting, many-speaker RTTM fixture is wanted for future testing,
  the current 30/60min fixtures should be replaced or clearly relabeled since they're
  concatenated benchmark clips, not meetings.

## Repro

```
swift build --package-path Tools/ProofHarness
swift run --package-path Tools/ProofHarness ProofHarness all \
  --fixtures-dir Data/diarization-fixtures --skip-summary --quality fast
```

Then compare `Data/diarization-fixtures/report.json` (`conversation[].speaker` /
`.startTime`, `speakerStats[]`) against `Data/diarization-fixtures/meeting-15min.rttm`
using a time-weighted overlap/purity calc (reference turns: `start dur ... speaker`
in RTTM column order).
EOF
)"

input.name: diar-empirical-pattern
input.description: Empirical failure-pattern analysis of diarization output
input.prompt:
Do an empirical, data-driven root-cause analysis of exactly how/where our diarization over-splits speakers, for issue #306.

Ground truth: `Data/diarization-fixtures/meeting-15min.rttm` (4 real speakers: FEO070, FEO072, MEE071, MEE073; RTTM columns are `SPEAKER file channel start dur <NA> <NA> speakerLabel <NA> <NA>`).

Predicted output: `Data/diarization-fixtures/report.json`, `results[3]` (file `meeting-15min.wav`) — `conversation[]` entries have `{text, speaker, startTime}`, no explicit endTime (reconstruct each turn's end as the next turn's startTime; the last turn ends at that result's `audioSeconds` value, 901.33).

I already computed time-weighted cluster purity for this fixture: 8 predicted speaker IDs map to 4 true speakers at 51.2% overall purity, with per-predicted-cluster purity ranging 34-69% (predicted IDs were 1,2,4,5,10,11,12,13).

Your job: build a merged, time-ordered timeline of (predicted-speaker-id, best-matching-true-speaker-by-overlap) across the whole meeting using Python (stdlib/pandas — read the two files directly, don't guess), and characterize the FAILURE PATTERN, not just the aggregate number. Specifically determine:

(a) Does over-splitting correlate with short segments — i.e. are the "extra" predicted IDs mostly tiny fragments (a few seconds), or do some carry substantial total time (tens of seconds+)?
(b) Does a single true speaker's predicted-ID assignment drift over the meeting duration (e.g. true speaker X is mostly predicted-ID 12 in the first half of the meeting but mostly predicted-ID 5 in the second half), suggesting embedding drift/instability over time rather than a bad initial cluster count?
(c) Do predicted-ID switches cluster right around true-speaker turn-change boundaries (suggesting turn-taking/silence-handling issues at speaker changes) or do they also happen randomly mid-turn (suggesting general embedding instability)?

Produce a concise report under 500 words stating which failure pattern(s) you found, with the supporting numbers/timeline evidence, since this determines whether the right fix is a clustering-threshold tweak, an embedding-window tweak, or something more structural (e.g. re-embedding per-turn vs streaming).

Investigation only — do not write or edit any production code; a throwaway Python analysis script is fine to write to a scratch location if useful, but the deliverable is the report.

<result>## Diarization failure-pattern analysis — `meeting-15min.wav` (issue #306)

Built a time-ordered timeline mapping each predicted turn to its best-overlap true speaker (RTTM), across all 8 predicted IDs vs 4 true speakers.

**(a) Not fragment noise — the extra IDs carry real duration.**
The 8 predicted IDs are not "1 real cluster + 7 junk slivers." Three carry the bulk (pred 12: 409.5s/41 segs, pred 11: 218.8s/39 segs, pred 13: 111.2s/22 segs = 82% of runtime), and even the "small" ones carry 12–73s across multiple multi-second segments (avg segment length 5–12s, not sub-second blips). This rules out a pure noise/fragmentation artifact — the system is confidently maintaining multiple competing clusters for what should be one speaker.

**(b) Temporal drift is real but speaker-specific, not universal.**
Splitting the meeting at the midpoint (450.7s):
- **MEE071 is rock-solid**: pred-ID 11 in both halves (57.4s / 59.0s). No drift, no confusion — proves the embedding *can* be stable for a full 15-min session.
- **FEO070 drifts hard**: first half mostly pred 1/11/10; second half mostly pred **12/13** — i.e. by the second half, FEO070's turns get absorbed into the cluster otherwise dominated by FEO072 (which sits on pred 12 the whole meeting). This is genuine embedding drift causing cross-speaker merging, not just splitting.
- **MEE073 is chronically unstable in both halves** (2/13/5 first half, 13/11/4 second half) — never settles on one ID even short-term. Looks like an inherently harder voice to embed consistently (possibly closer acoustic proximity to MEE071/FEO072, or more crosstalk/overlap on this speaker's turns) rather than a drift-over-time story.

**(c) Switches split roughly 70/30 between turn boundaries and mid-turn.**
125 total pred-ID switches: 86 (69%) land within 1.0s of an actual RTTM speaker-turn boundary; 39 (31%) happen with no true boundary nearby (median distance 0.62s, max 4.2s from switches that *are* boundary-adjacent). So most re-clustering failures happen exactly at real speaker changes (the system spins up a new ID instead of re-matching to an existing speaker's centroid), but a meaningful third of instability is pure mid-utterance embedding noise with no speaker change at all.

**Conclusion — not a simple "raise the cluster threshold" fix.** Three distinct failure modes are present simultaneously: (1) turn-boundary re-identification failure (majority, 69% of switches) — new speaker turns not matched back to existing cluster centroids; (2) mid-turn embedding instability (31% of switches) — same speaker, ID flips without a real change; (3) speaker-specific cross-contamination (FEO070↔FEO072) that's a matching/threshold problem, not fragmentation. A blanket threshold loosening risks merging the currently-correct MEE071 while still not fixing MEE073's chronic instability or FEO070's drift. Investigation should split into: embedding window/smoothing (mid-turn stability), centroid re-matching logic at turn boundaries (streaming vs. re-embed-and-compare), and per-speaker acoustic similarity (why FEO070/FEO072 specifically confuse).</result>

**Key finding: it's not one bug, it's three distinct failure modes happening at once.**

**Bottom line from this agent**: a blanket "loosen the clustering threshold" fix is risky — it would likely merge `MEE071` (currently correct) while still not fixing `MEE073`'s instability or the `FEO070`/`FEO072` cross-contamination. The real fix needs to be split three ways: turn-boundary re-matching logic, mid-turn embedding smoothing, and per-speaker acoustic-similarity handling.

<result>## Report: FluidAudio Diarization Tuning — Issue #306

### Part 1 — Built-in DER/purity scoring (YES, it exists)

**`DiarizationDER`** (`Sources/FluidAudio/Diarizer/DiarizationDER.swift`) is a **public** API in the main `FluidAudio` library target — directly importable by `Tools/ProofHarness` today, no new dependency needed. It implements the standard pyannote/NIST md-eval DER formula (miss + false-alarm + confusion, Hungarian-matched hyp→ref mapping, configurable collar). Input type is `DERSpeakerSegment(speaker:start:end:)`; output is `DERResult(der:confusion:falseAlarm:miss:totalRefSpeech:mapping:)` — the `mapping` field is exactly the cluster-purity signal issue #306 needs (which hyp cluster the Hungarian solver assigned to which true speaker, and which hyp clusters got no match = pure over-segmentation).

A richer, segment-overlap-based version — `DiarizationMetricsCalculator.offlineMetrics()` in `Sources/FluidAudioCLI/Utils/DiarizationMetrics.swift` — adds JER and per-rate breakdowns (missRate/falseAlarmRate/speakerErrorRate), but it's **internal to the `FluidAudioCLI` executable target**, not exported from the library, so it can't be imported directly — porting the ~150-line algorithm (or copying the file) would be needed to use it.

**Wiring plan**: `ProofHarness` already has `FluidDiarizationPlugin` output as `[SpeakerSegment]`; map those + parsed `.rttm` ground truth into `[DERSpeakerSegment]` and call `DiarizationDER.compute(ref:hyp:)` directly. One gap: FluidAudio's RTTM parser (`RTTMParser.loadSegments`) also lives only in `FluidAudioCLI`, not the library — ProofHarness needs its own trivial RTTM line parser (~15 lines) or a copy of that file.

### Part 2 — Upstream config knobs + precedent

Repo: `https://github.com/FluidInference/FluidAudio` (pinned rev `8048812...`, v0.14.7 per `Package.resolved`).

Found the exact tunable in `OfflineDiarizerTypes.swift`: `OfflineDiarizerConfig.Clustering`:
```swift
public static let community = Clustering(
    threshold: 0.6,       // Euclidean distance on unit-normalized embeddings
    warmStartFa: 0.07, warmStartFb: 0.8,
    minSpeakers: nil, maxSpeakers: nil, numSpeakers: nil
)
```
`minSpeakers`/`maxSpeakers`/`numSpeakers` are direct config overrides on the same struct — since our fixtures have known ground truth (4 speakers), setting `maxSpeakers: 4` (or `numSpeakers: 4`) is a zero-risk immediate mitigation for the fixture benchmark, independent of threshold tuning.

**Direct upstream precedent for our exact symptom**: FluidAudio's own benchmark docs/tables show mismatched-threshold over-segmentation on AMI meetings that mirrors #306's ratio almost exactly — e.g. `ES2004a: 7 predicted vs 4 actual`, `IS1002b: 9 predicted vs 4 actual`. Upstream guidance: **lower threshold → more/smaller clusters (over-segmentation)**, **higher threshold → fewer/merged clusters**. Default `0.6` targets ~18–20% DER on AMI-SDM (offline/VBx pipeline); an older non-VBx pipeline used `0.7` for ~17.7% DER. Given our 8-vs-4 result, the first experiment to run is raising `threshold` from `0.6` toward `0.7`–`0.8` on `meeting-15min.wav`, in combination with (or instead of) an explicit `maxSpeakers` cap.

   - **`Tools/ProofHarness`**: standalone Swift CLI package (own `Package.swift`, separate `.build` from the monorepo root) with `ArgumentParser` subcommands `Run` (single WAV), `RunAll`/`all` (all WAVs in a fixtures dir), `Compare` (MLX vs XGrammar summarization comparison), `List` (list fixtures with rttm/json badges), `SummarizeText`. Not part of the main monorepo `swift build`/`swift test`, so it can silently drift out of sync with library API changes (as happened here).
   - **`PipelineRunner`** (`Tools/ProofHarness/Sources/PipelineRunner.swift`): orchestrates the real pipeline — instantiates and calls actual production plugins: `ParakeetPlugin()`, `WhisperKitPlugin()`, `FluidDiarizationPlugin()`, `XGrammarSummarizationPlugin()`, `MLXSummarizationPlugin()`, `SentenceAligner.align(...)` — the same classes wired into `AppAssembler`/`TranscriptionSubAssembler` in the shipping app. Method signature involved: `runner.run(wavURL:quality:skipSummary:summaryModelId:) async throws -> PipelineResult`.

# Finish 3 escalated dead-feature issues (#300, #301, #302)

## Context

The #216 composition-root audit surfaced three features whose engine/store/use-case layers
already exist and are real, but which are never wired to a consumer — so they don't function
in the shipping app. Each was escalated to its own issue. The user chose to **build all three
as real features** (not delete). Design forks resolved with the user:

- **#300** — enroll speakers **from an existing recording** (pick meeting → pick a diarized
  speaker → name → enroll), and **auto-apply matching in the pipeline** (relabel generic
  "Speaker N" with enrolled names on every new recording).
- **#301** — implement a real `LiveDataEraser`, wire it in, re-enable the disabled button.
- **#302** — implement the real 3-node LLM DAG and surface a **"Generate Business Plan"**
  Pro action in meeting detail.

Layer rule (hard constraint): Presentation imports **Business + Domain only, never
Infrastructure**. All three consumers are Presentation VMs; the concrete engines live in
Infrastructure/RecordPro and must reach the VM either as a Business use case or via a
Domain-defined protocol. `AppAssembler` is the only place concrete types are constructed.

Ship order: **#301 → #300 → #302** (ascending risk). Each is an independent branch + PR,
one commit per logical unit, verified with `swift build` + full `swift test` before commit.

---

## #301 — LiveDataEraser (lowest risk; consumer + contract already exist)

Consumer already exists and compiles against the `DataEraser` protocol
(`Record-Foundation/.../Domain/Storage/DataEraser.swift`): `SettingsViewModel.performDeleteAllData(dataEraser:)`
+ the (disabled) button in `SettingsViewDeleteAllSection.swift`. Only the producer + wiring are missing.

**Producer** — new `Record-App/Sources/TheRecord/LiveDataEraser.swift` (App layer, where the
concrete stores are known), `struct LiveDataEraser: DataEraser`. `eraseAllData()` deletes, in
order, returning a label per resource actually removed (matches protocol doc — returns `[String]`,
throws `DataEraseError.partialFailure` on any failure):
  1. WAV recordings — enumerate via `RecordingReadRepository`, delete each `metadata.audioURL` file.
  2. GRDB database — close the pool (`GRDBStorageActor.close()`) then remove the DB file at
     `Directories.appSupport / AppConstants.Paths.databaseFileName` (+ `-wal`/`-shm` siblings).
  3. Context cache / commitment stores — their DB files (`GRDBContextCache`, `GRDBCommitmentStore`).
  4. Keychain credentials — `CredentialStore` (`Record-ML/.../Security/CredentialStore.swift`).
  5. App preferences — the config manager's persisted settings (`sharedConfigManager`).
  Collect labels; if any step throws, accumulate and throw `.partialFailure(paths:)` at the end.

**Wire** — `App.swift` Settings scene: pass a real `LiveDataEraser(...)` into `SettingsView`
(add a `dataEraser` param to `SettingsView.init`, thread it to `deleteAllDataSection`). Delete the
hardcoded `NoOpDataEraser()` bridge in `SettingsViewDeleteAllSection.swift` and re-enable the button:
replace `.disabled(true)` with `.disabled(!viewModel.isDeleteAllConfirmed || !viewModel.isDeleteAllDataEnabled)`
(the commented-out line already there). Keep `NoOpDataEraser` only if still needed for previews/tests.

**Tests (RED first)** — `LiveDataEraser` unit test with a temp app-support dir + in-memory/temp
GRDB: seed a recording WAV + DB rows, run `eraseAllData()`, assert files gone and labels returned;
negative path: unwritable resource → `.partialFailure`. Existing `SettingsViewModelDeleteAllTests`
already covers the VM orchestration.

---

## #300 — Speaker enrollment + auto-matching

Real pieces already present: `VoiceEmbedding` (genuine mel/FFT math), `VoiceEmbeddingActor`
(`Record-ML/.../Speaker/VoiceEmbedding.swift`), `JSONSpeakerProfileStore` (already assembled as
`speakerProfileStore` since #216), `EnrollSpeakerUseCase` + `MatchSpeakersUseCase`
(`Record-App/Sources/Business/UseCases/`, both real, Business layer → reachable by Presentation).
Missing: construction in the assembler, an enrollment UI, and the pipeline match hook.

**Assembler** — in `AppAssembler.assemble()` (or `AppAssemblerBuilders`) construct once:
`let voiceEmbedding = VoiceEmbeddingActor()`, `let enrollSpeaker = EnrollSpeakerUseCase(store: speakerProfileStore, embedding: voiceEmbedding)`,
`let matchSpeakers = MatchSpeakersUseCase(store: speakerProfileStore, embedding: voiceEmbedding)`.

**Auto-matching hook (least-invasive)** — inject `matchSpeakers: MatchSpeakersUseCase?` into
`DiarizeMeetingUseCase` (new optional init param; construction site
`TranscriptionSubAssembler.swift:103`). At the end of `diarize(...)`, when non-nil, return
`try await matchSpeakers.labelDiarization(diarizedTranscript, audioSamples: samples, sampleRate: 16000)`
— reuses the samples DiarizeMeetingUseCase already loaded; `PipelineCoordinator` untouched.

**Enrollment UI (consumer)** — in the existing **Speakers tab**
(`SettingsViewTranscriptionTab.swift:35` `speakersTab`, VM `SettingsViewModel` +
`SettingsViewModelAudio.swift`). Add:
  - `SettingsViewModel` deps: `enrollSpeaker: EnrollSpeakerUseCase?`, `audioSampleLoader: (any AudioSampleLoader)?`
    (Business/Domain types — layer-safe). `recordingReadRepository` already present.
  - VM method `enrollSpeaker(fromRecording:speakerId:name:)`: load segments for the recording,
    `audioSampleLoader.loadSamples(from: audioURL)`, slice each `DiarizedSegment` for that
    `speakerId` (`startTime*16000 ..< endTime*16000`), concatenate until ≥16000 samples, call
    `enrollSpeaker.enroll(name:samples:)`, then `loadProfiles()`. Surface `SpeakerError`
    (invalidName / insufficientAudio / duplicateName) via `errorMessage`.
  - UI: an "Enroll from meeting" disclosure in `speakersTab` — meeting picker (recent recordings)
    → speaker picker (distinct speakerIds in that recording's segments) → name field → Enroll.
  - `App.swift` Settings scene: pass `enrollSpeaker` + `AudioFileLoader()` into `SettingsViewModel`.

**Tests (RED first)** — VM enroll test with a mock store + mock loader + a fixture recording:
assert profile created, insufficient-audio path throws, duplicate-name path surfaces error.
`DiarizeMeetingUseCase` test: with an injected match use case, generic labels get relabeled to
enrolled names; without it, output unchanged (nil path).

---

## #302 — Business Plan guided generation (highest risk; no consumer today)

`BusinessPlanSkill` + 3 `GuidedAgentNode` conformers exist but are dummy scaffolds with zero
consumers. `RecordPro` depends on `Domain` + `MLInfrastructure`, so `SummarizationEngine`
(`generate(prompt:)`, unified in #214/#215) and `SchemaGenerator` are both reachable. Presentation
does **not** import RecordPro → need a Domain-owned protocol boundary (mirror the
`TranscriptRepairService` pattern: protocol in Domain, conformer in RecordPro, use case in Business).

**Domain** — new `BusinessPlanGenerator` protocol:
`func generatePlan(from transcript: String) async throws -> String` (returns rendered markdown,
keeping `BusinessPlanSchema` an internal RecordPro detail — no cross-layer type move).

**RecordPro producer** — rewrite `BusinessPlanDAG.swift` nodes to take an injected
`any SummarizationEngine` and call `engine.generate(prompt:)`:
  - Extractor: `extractorSystemPrompt` + transcript → loose facts string.
  - Corrector: `correctorSystemPrompt` + extracted → formatted string.
  - Verifier: `verifierSystemPrompt` + corrected + `SchemaGenerator.generate(from:)` schema →
    JSON → decode `BusinessPlanSchema`.
  Add `BusinessPlanSkill(engine:)`; conform `BusinessPlanSkill: BusinessPlanGenerator` by rendering
  the resulting `BusinessPlanSchema` (12 sections) to markdown. Ensure model is loaded
  (`isReady()` / `loadModel`) as `ProTranscriptRepairService` does.

**Business use case** — `GenerateBusinessPlanUseCase(generator: any BusinessPlanGenerator)` wrapping
the Domain protocol (mirrors `RepairTranscriptUseCase`).

**Presentation consumer** — `MeetingDetailViewModel` gets
`generateBusinessPlanUseCase: GenerateBusinessPlanUseCase?` (optional, like `repairUseCase`),
`businessPlanMarkdown: String?`, and `func generateBusinessPlan()` running on `transcript`.
Add a **"Generate Business Plan"** button in `BroadsheetDockBar.swift` (shown only when the use
case is non-nil — the Pro gate), display the markdown result (reuse MarkdownUI rendering used for
summaries) with a loading state, and allow copy/export.

**Assembler** — construct `BusinessPlanSkill(engine: repairEngine)` (reuse the already-resolved
`transcriptionBuilt?.summarizationEngine ?? MLXSummarizationPlugin()` used for repair at
`AppAssembler.swift:136`), wrap in `GenerateBusinessPlanUseCase`, inject into `MeetingDetailViewModel`.

**Tests (RED first)** — RecordPro integration test: `BusinessPlanSkill(engine: mockEngine)`
`.generatePlan(from:)` runs all 3 stages against a scripted mock engine and returns markdown
containing all 12 section headings; verifier decode-failure path surfaces an error.

---

## Verification (each issue)

- `swift build` clean + full `swift test` green (currently 1019 tests / 168 suites) before every commit.
- **App gate** (per build-order rule — UI features need eyes-on): launch the app, and for
  - #301: type DELETE, confirm button enables, run erase on a throwaway recording, verify files gone.
  - #300: enroll a speaker from a recording, run a new recording through the pipeline, confirm
    diarized segments show the enrolled name instead of "Speaker N".
  - #302: open a meeting with a transcript, hit Generate Business Plan, confirm a 12-section plan renders.
- One commit per logical unit; branches `fix/301-live-data-eraser`, `fix/300-speaker-enroll-match`,
  `fix/302-business-plan`. Local-only until the user asks to push/PR (same flow as #298/#299/#303).
- If any producer's real behavior can't be exercised end-to-end (e.g. model not downloaded for #302),
  say so explicitly rather than claiming success.

---

I want you to solve this problem:

Our diarization pipeline over-splits speakers. On `Data/diarization-fixtures/meeting-15min.wav` (4 real ground-truth speakers: `FEO070`, `FEO072`, `MEE071`, `MEE073`, per `meeting-15min.rttm`), `FluidDiarizationPlugin` (`Record-ML/Sources/MLInfrastructure/Diarization/FluidDiarizationPlugin.swift`) produces **8 predicted speaker clusters** at **51.2% time-weighted purity**. Full writeup, methodology, and fixture-validity caveats are in **GitHub issue #306**. Three investigation angles have already been run and their reports are pasted below — read them before touching anything.

The result I want is:

Diarization purity/DER improved on `meeting-15min.wav` (target: purity meaningfully above 51%, with `MEE071` — currently the one stable speaker — not regressed by whatever change is made), **plus** an automated purity/DER check wired into `Tools/ProofHarness` so this class of regression gets caught by every future fixture run instead of requiring a manual Python script. A tuning change that isn't measured against the RTTM ground truth doesn't count as done.

Use these sources:

- GitHub issue #306 (full problem statement, methodology, fixture-validity notes on why `meeting-30min`/`meeting-60min` RTTMs are unusable — they're VoxPopuli clips spliced onto the real 4-speaker conversation, not real ground truth).
- `Record-ML/Sources/MLInfrastructure/Diarization/FluidDiarizationPlugin.swift` — our wrapper.
- Vendored FluidAudio source at `Record-Foundation/.build-task2/checkouts/FluidAudio/` (v0.14.7, pinned rev `8048812...`) — in particular `Sources/FluidAudio/Diarizer/OfflineDiarizerTypes.swift` (`Clustering.community` config: `threshold: 0.6`, plus `minSpeakers`/`maxSpeakers`/`numSpeakers` overrides), `DiarizationDER.swift` (public, importable DER scorer — Hungarian-matched hyp→ref mapping, exactly the signal we need), and `Sources/FluidAudioCLI/Utils/DiarizationMetrics.swift` (richer offline metrics, but internal to the CLI target — would need porting).
- `Data/diarization-fixtures/` — `meeting-15min.wav` + `.rttm` (the only trustworthy fixture) plus `report.json` from the latest full pipeline run.
- `Tools/ProofHarness/` — the standalone CLI harness (own `Package.swift`, not part of the main monorepo build/test) where automated scoring should be wired in.
- Investigation report 1 — empirical failure-pattern analysis:
  > Not fragment noise — the 8 predicted IDs carry real duration (5–12s avg segments, 3 IDs = 82% of runtime). `MEE071` is rock-solid on one predicted ID the entire meeting (proves stable embeddings are possible). `FEO070` drifts hard mid-meeting and gets absorbed into `FEO072`'s cluster in the second half — genuine cross-speaker contamination, not just splitting. `MEE073` never settles in either half of the meeting — chronic instability, likely an acoustically-similar-voice problem. 69% of the 125 ID switches land within 1s of a real speaker-turn boundary (re-identification failure — new turn not matched back to an existing centroid); 31% happen mid-utterance with no real speaker change (pure embedding noise). Conclusion: **three distinct failure modes, not one bug** — a blanket threshold loosen risks merging the currently-correct `MEE071` while not fixing `MEE073`'s instability or the `FEO070`/`FEO072` contamination.
- Investigation report 2 — upstream FluidAudio research:
  > FluidAudio ships a public `DiarizationDER` API we can call directly from `ProofHarness` today (no new dependency) — needs a small RTTM parser (~15 lines) since FluidAudio's own parser is CLI-internal. First experiment to run: raise `threshold` toward `0.7`–`0.8` and compare against an explicit `maxSpeakers` cap.

- Local-only git operations (commit/branch) — no push, no PR, unless explicitly asked.

Our diarization pipeline over-splits speakers. Diarization purity/DER improved on `meeting-15min.wav` (target: purity meaningfully above 51%, with `MEE071` — currently the one stable speaker — not regressed by whatever change is made), **plus** an automated purity/DER check wired into `Tools/ProofHarness` so this class of regression gets caught by every future fixture run instead of requiring a manual Python script. Confirmed at runtime: `speakerThreshold = clusteringThreshold * 1.2 = 0.84` (max cosine distance to match an existing speaker), `embeddingThreshold = clusteringThreshold * 0.8 = 0.56` (max distance to refresh a profile) — a separate hardcoded `AssignmentConfig.macOS` (0.65/0.45) exists but is **not** the path our code exercises. **Biggest structural finding**: FluidAudio ships two diarizers — the streaming `DiarizerManager` we use, and `OfflineDiarizerManager` (VBx clustering, benchmarked 17.7% DER on AMI), purpose-built for full-recording batch processing. Our use case (record full meeting, process after the fact) is inherently offline — **we may be running the wrong engine for the job.**
  >
  > Ranked recommendations: (1) evaluate swapping to `OfflineDiarizerManager` — biggest expected accuracy win, but an engine swap not a config tweak, bigger integration lift; (2) raise `clusteringThreshold` 0.7→~0.8-0.85 via a custom `DiarizerConfig` passed to `DiarizerManager(config:)` — cheapest single-line experiment, confirmed direction (raises match cutoff, makes merges easier, directly counteracts over-splitting) — try first; (3) lower `minEmbeddingUpdateDuration` 2.0s→1.0-1.5s — real meetings have sub-2s backchannel turns ("yeah," "right") that never refresh a speaker's reference embedding, causing later utterances to drift into a "new speaker" against a stale anchor — needs A/B validation, could also let noisy short segments corrupt profiles; (4) pass an explicit `numClusters: 4` hint for diagnostic-only runs (ground truth is known for this fixture) to isolate cluster-count vs. distance-threshold as the dominant cause before committing to #2/#3.
